scope.boundary: Aggregate rates do not reveal the rater/seed/state allocation or dependence, so evidence fractions are sensitivity devices.
scope.model: Independent binomial cell likelihoods with Beta priors and equal task weighting. Simulator evidence is discounted from 60 labels to 30 rollout or 10 initial-state equivalents.
scope.source_structure: 10 real initial states per policy-task; three Cosmos seeds per initial state; two manual raters per generated rollout.

oscar_public_join.scope: Source-discrepancy diagnostic only. The joined real outcomes cover the 63 released session IDs, while the printed world-model bars imply 65 sessions and the printed real bars use another unstated RoboArena aggregation. The cross-vector correlation and regret are not an exact matched-session evaluator estimate.

scope.boundary: Episode pairing, checkpoint dependence, and training-run structure are unreleased. Evidence discounting is a stress device, not an estimated effective sample size.

decision_atlas.real_trial_remeasurement_scope: Model-conditional real-trial measurement uncertainty for cases with documented real denominators; simulator values held fixed where simulator rollout counts are unavailable. rows.primary_source_basis: Abstract; Fig. 1; Section III-A: simulation is presented as predicting real performance over evaluated policies.
Introduction and Section 5.3: DROID training followed by RoboArena evaluation beyond training environments; held-out trajectories and trial-count analysis.
Abstract and real-to-sim correlation section: generated cousins are validated against real outcomes across architectures and generalization levels.
Abstract and Fig. 1: purpose-built simulation is evaluated as a proxy for real policy performance; MMRV and behavior-mode validation accompany correlation.
Abstract; Section 5.1; Tables 2 and G.8: multiple tasks and architectures with separate held-out task and object evaluations.
Abstract and Section 4.1: relative policy rankings are real-validated; OOD tasks are evaluated only in the world model.
Abstract and Sections 4.3-4.5: single-image reconstruction and real-task correlation; replay uses selected scenes while the coefficient roster remains fixed.
Abstract and Sections III-IV: a named seven-skill/fifteen-perturbation benchmark with nearly 800 paired rollouts.
Section 5.2: co-training uses 15 held-out simulation environments and evaluation targets unseen environments; policies/tasks are described as representative.
Abstract and Sections 3.3/4.4: seven policies and a task semantic absent from training; per-chunk uncertainty is explicitly not a calibrated probability.
Introduction and Section 4: unseen environments, objects, and tasks are tested; limitations leave substantially novel cases unresolved.
Abstract and Section 5 limitation: finite policies/tasks support measured ranking and correlation comparisons but not definitive simulator or policy ranking.
Abstract and Fig. 1: evaluator is intended to select promising policies for real evaluation or deployment while retaining real validation as a final step.
Abstract and Sections 3-4: 1600+ paired real evaluations across eight checkpoints, five tasks, nominal and edited OOD axes.
Abstract and Section 4.7: held-out validation and OOD benchmarks accompany a six-checkpoint correlation panel.
Abstract; Section 4.3; Fig. 7: heterogeneous policies and task domains include physical real panels without a defined policy/task population.
Abstract and policy-evaluation section: five real manipulation tasks; reward prediction is also checked on held-out real trajectories.
Abstract and Sections 3.1/4: 500+ clips from 20+ policies and held-out objects; play data are argued to approximate broad policy-outcome coverage.
Abstract and Section 5: captured deployment environments use randomly sampled start-goal episodes across four fixed policy variants.
Abstract and Section 5.2: formal train/validation/test splits and random scene samples in secondary analyses; the coefficient panel remains selected.
Abstract; Section 4.2; Fig. 4: a fixed two-policy/five-task real comparison supports evaluator and post-training claims.
Abstract and Section V-F: 28 tasks and 16 controlled perturbations with hardware trend validation; the hardware coefficient uses one policy.
Abstract and Section 6.2: a standardized realistic benchmark with real validation for fixed Octo/OpenVLA task rosters.
Abstract and Section 5.4: RoboArena policy evaluation supports future virtual evaluation; held-out human data diagnose generation rather than define the seven-policy population.
Abstract; Section 4.2.3; RQ4: evaluator correlation plus held-out appearance/background/distractor tests.
Abstract and Section IV-C: fixed synthetic and Bridge panels; the formulation invokes a representative task set without a sampling rule.

wm_heterogeneous_simulator_evidence.scope: Posterior latent-rank concordance under independent Beta cells and policy-specific effective evidence shared across four tasks. Not operational selection reliability or an estimate of actual evidence/dependence.

wm_missing_simulator_sensitivity.scope: Finite retained WM-PolicyEval panels under independent Beta-binomial cell sensitivities with one common effective simulator evidence size for every policy-task cell. The estimand is posterior concordance between independently sampled latent simulator-best and real-best policies, not reliability of an observed-data operational action. With common positive evidence and a symmetric prior, the posterior-mean simulator action is unchanged because every displayed rate receives the same positive affine transform. Evidence sizes are not estimates of the missing simulator denominator and results do not transport.

wm_nonlinear_calibration.scope: Full-panel in-sample equal-cell isotonic shape sensitivity and finite forecast-level Murphy decomposition; not prospective calibration, selection repair, or transport evidence.

wm_probability_calibration.boundary: Twelve outcome-exposed cells per evaluator, four task deletion folds, unknown simulator denominator, and no task/policy sampling frame.
wm_probability_calibration.interpretation: Probability-level fit adds an orthogonal descriptive axis on these retained panels. Positive affine recalibration preserves the aggregate selection, so it neither repairs nor creates the argmax result.
